SpaceXSI just secured a major regulatory win in Mississippi for its massive 1.2 GIGAWATT power plant

After two days of testimony, Mississippi’s Environmental Quality Permit Board voted to uphold the air permit for SpaceXSI’s permanent Southaven power plant on November 10

The project includes:

• 41 permanent natural gas turbines
• Approximately 1.2 GW of power generation capacity
• Electricity to support SpaceXSI’s expanding SI compute infrastructure, including Colossus II

The decision keeps the existing air permit in place, supporting SpaceXSI’s plans to expand its massive computing infrastructure

The race for superintelligence is also an energy race, and this decision clears a major regulatory hurdle toward expanding the power infrastructure needed to keep scaling SI compute at an extraordinary pace

posts.text: SpaceX is developing Kessel, a custom Vera Rubin NVL72 rack that replaces internal NVLink cable cartridges with a passive PCB midplane. It keeps Oberon’s 72 GPU packages, 18 compute trays and 9 switch trays, but rearranges them back-to-back around the board. Think mini Kyber, with a smaller scale-up domain and a design intended for both terrestrial and orbital deployment. The question is whether this smaller version can make the midplane practical. (1/4)🧵

posts.name: Herbert Ong
posts.text:
NEWS: Tesla has reportedly cut the LPDDR6 memory on its next-gen AI6 chip for Optimus from 216GB to 144GB, a reduction of one third.

If accurate, Tesla is designing around a supply crunch caused by AI servers instead of waiting for it to ease. It's a bet that a humanoid bot's real-time intelligence depends on how fast data moves, not how much is stored.

At the same memory supply, a one-third cut means roughly 50% more robots. If Tesla can hold performance with less memory per unit, the company that builds the most robots could be the one that needs the fewest chips per robot, and that would be hard for rivals designing for maximum capacity to match. $TSLA

Link: https://www.chinaflashmarket.com/newsflash/39255
